source.title: MADAR: An Address-Free Processor
source.summary: In a modern processor, computing is the cheap part. Most of its area and energy go to \emph{addressing} -- moving operands to and from a register file and cache, and running the tags, ports, miss queues, and bypass networks that find a value where it was left. MADAR deletes that machinery by abolishing the address. All state circulates in rings of slots that advance one position per clock; instructions and data ride in the same slots; a value is named by its place in an orbit -- a \rp{} coordinate -- not by an address; a fixed station computes when a circulating instruction sweeps past its operands, on a schedule set at compile time; and a hierarchy of rings of increasing period replaces the cache hierarchy, movement between them scheduled rather than triggered by a miss. No prior circulating-store, dataflow, or statically scheduled machine combines all four of these. We define the execution model, validate it in a cycle-accurate register-transfer-level implementation, show it \emph{compilable} -- a constructive scheduler emits programs cross-checked against the implementation -- and price it with a first-order energy model. The payoff is clearest for AI acceleration: the multiply-accumulate at the heart of every matmul and convolution compiles to a streaming form whose energy per operation stays flat as the reduction grows, and the operand reuse that makes matrix multiplication efficient is carried by the ring-period hierarchy -- the memory hierarchy doing by rotation what a cache does by tags. MADAR is a new design point for any computation whose data movement is known before the program runs.

previous_facts.title: MADAR: An Address-Free Processor
previous_facts.event_hint: MADAR: a proposed address-free processor architecture that abolishes random-access storage and the program counter, replacing them with a single primitive (rotation): all state circulates in a compile-time-scheduled hierarchy of rings of increasing period, with fixed compute stations executing instructions when they sweep past their operands; validated only via a cycle-accurate RTL implementation and a first-order energy model, with no silicon or hardware measurements.
previous_facts.problem: In a modern processor, computing (arithmetic) is the cheap part; most area and energy go to addressing — moving operands to/from a register file and cache, and running the tags, ports, miss queues, and bypass networks that find a value where it was left. A cited detailed energy measurement of a general-purpose processor running a video encoder reports functional units consumed under 6% of total energy, with >90% being overhead relative to the operations actually performed, and instruction supply alone roughly a third of core energy. The tension: the datapath streams operands through functional units, but the memory system forces every value to rest at a fixed address so it can be found again on demand, requiring register files with many ports, caches with tag arrays/MSHRs, memory arbiters, load-store queues, and operand-bypass networks.
previous_facts.mechanism: MADAR replaces the von Neumann primitives (random-access store + program counter) with a single primitive: rotation. Four conjoined properties: (a) Circulating storage — the only storage is a set of rings R0..Rn, each a circular sequence of slots advancing one slot per clock, with geometrically increasing periods (representative values 16, 256, 4K, 64K slots); small fast rings are literal shift registers, large slow rings are single-port SRAM banks read/written through a rotating pointer (sequential, portless access with no address decode/tags/arbitration/multi-porting). (b) Co-circulating code and data — every slot holds one packet (64-bit payload + kind tag, or opcode + operand refs + destination + predicate); instructions and data ride in the same slots, distinguished only by a kind field. (c) Distributed collision execution — fixed compute stations (ALU, multiplier, steer, transfer, I/O) mounted at fixed ring positions; an instruction executes when it sweeps past a station of its class, with operands named by rotational offset within a window W=8 slots ahead; no queue, no scheduler, no dynamic matching, no scoreboard, no wakeup (arrival is the schedule). (d) Compiler-scheduled period hierarchy — a hierarchy of rings of increasing period replaces the cache hierarchy; transfer stations bridge adjacent rings (promoting/demoting values) on a compile-time schedule, doing by rotation what a cache does by tags, with no reactive misses. The constructive scheduler emits programs cross-checked against the cycle-accurate RTL. A rendezvous station (one comparator against one free-running phase counter) handles values the schedule cannot pre-place, at the cost of ~half a rotation of latency.

evidence.claim: Architecture validation method (abstract + Section 5/7): MADAR is validated in a cycle-accurate register-transfer-level (RTL) implementation (programs cross-checked against the implementation by a constructive scheduler) and priced with a FIRST-ORDER energy model. There is no silicon, no tape-out, no FPGA prototype, and no hardware benchmark; all performance/energy figures are model-derived, not measured.
evidence.value: cycle-accurate RTL + first-order energy model; no silicon/measurements
evidence.condition: representative working ring parameters (periods 16/256/4K/64K); no physical implementation
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 1 (Abstract); PDF Page 8 (Section 7 cost model, Threats to validity)

evidence.claim: Motivating energy claim (cited prior measurement, Section 1): in a detailed energy measurement of a general-purpose processor running a video encoder, functional units consumed under 6% of total energy and >90% was overhead relative to the operations actually performed; instruction supply is roughly a third of core energy. This is the external motivation for deleting addressing machinery and supplying loop bodies for free (a parked loop body re-executes once per revolution with no fetch/decode/branch prediction).
evidence.value: FU <6% of energy; >90% overhead; instruction supply ~1/3 of core energy
evidence.baseline: conventional general-purpose processor (video encoder workload, cited [12])
evidence.condition: cited prior detailed energy measurement, not a MADAR measurement

evidence.claim: Design-rationale deletions (Section 3): MADAR deletes (rather than optimizes) addressing machinery — no tags (slot identity is its phase), no arbitration (one packet per slot per cycle), a single sequential SRAM port swept by a rotating pointer (no random address decode, no port replication), no MSHRs (nothing requested reactively), and the W=8 operand window replaces the bypass network. Timing is exact (emitted schedule == executed schedule cycle-for-cycle), distinguishing it from statically scheduled VLIW whose bundles issue against a reactive register file/caches where a miss invalidates the schedule.
evidence.value: deletes tags/arbitration/MSHRs/multi-ports/bypass-network; exact cycle-true scheduling vs VLIW reactive stalls
evidence.baseline: conventional von Neumann core; statically scheduled VLIW

evidence.claim: Streaming AI inference case study (Section 8): the inference primitives (dot product, streaming inner product, matmul tile) were built, compiled, and validated against the cycle-accurate model and priced with the cost model. A flat reduction tree does not seat under the constructive scheduler (products scatter beyond the W=8 window); written as a sequential accumulation s_i = s_{i-1} + a_i*b_i the scheduler seats it with no relays. The win is real where the ring is sized to the work; operand reuse (the heart of matmul efficiency) routes through the period hierarchy; the MAC compiles to a streaming form whose energy per operation the authors claim stays flat as the reduction grows.
evidence.value: sequential accumulation seats with no relays; flat reduction loses; MAC energy/op claimed flat as reduction grows
evidence.condition: MADAR cycle-accurate RTL + first-order cost model; matmul tile primitives
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 8 (Section 8 A Case Study: Streaming AI Inference)

evidence.claim: Threats to validity (Section 7): the cost model is first-order — its gated rotation is an idealized clock-gate (counts slots whose contents change, not a measured flop-enable network); it prices a rotation by one per-word figure rather than a synthesized netlist; the baseline is a single published per-instruction number, not a matched implementation measured on the same flow. The authors state the figures are stand-ins and the result they rest on is the crossover (robust to exact magnitudes), not an absolute energy; a synthesis-based comparison of both machines through one flow is the evaluation this model motivates and does not replace.
evidence.value: first-order model; idealized clock-gate; single per-word rotation price; single published baseline number; no synthesized netlist
evidence.baseline: single published per-instruction energy number (not matched)

previous_facts.evaluation_context: Implementation: cycle-accurate register-transfer-level (RTL) model of the MADAR execution engine, with a constructive scheduler that emits programs cross-checked against the RTL. Pricing: a first-order energy model (idealized gated rotation counting changed slots; one per-word rotation price; no synthesized netlist; baseline is a single published per-instruction energy number, not a matched implementation). Representative ring parameters: periods 16/256/4K/64K slots; operand window W=8; packet = 64-bit payload + 2-bit kind + 3-bit opcode + 4-bit src_a/src_b/dst. Case study: dot product, streaming inner product, matmul tile compiled and validated against the cycle-accurate model and priced with the cost model. External motivation: a cited detailed energy measurement of a conventional GP processor running a video encoder (FU <6%, >90% overhead, instruction supply ~1/3 of core energy). No silicon, tape-out, FPGA, or hardware benchmark; no comparison against a matched synthesized baseline of a conventional machine.
previous_facts.limitations: This is an architecture proposal with NO physical implementation: no silicon, no tape-out, no FPGA prototype, no hardware measurements. All performance and energy properties are model-derived (cycle-accurate RTL + first-order energy model). The authors explicitly state the energy figures are stand-ins and the robust result is the crossover (not absolute energy); the baseline is a single published per-instruction number rather than a matched implementation measured on the same flow, and a synthesis-based comparison is the evaluation this model motivates and does NOT replace. The AI-inference case study covers only micro-primitives (dot product, inner product, matmul tile), not full models, real workloads, or end-to-end throughput/latency against a real accelerator. The W=8 operand window is a hard reach limit: producers and consumers more than 8 slots apart require compiler-emitted XFER relay chains that occupy slots, so long-range dependences trade against ring capacity (a chain of 24 at 72 packets no longer fits a 64-slot ring); dense kernels may fail to fit. The architecture is suited only to computations whose data movement is known before the program runs (Section 9 bound); data-dependent/control-flow-heavy workloads are out of scope. No HBM/HBF/interconnect/package data; no TOPS/TFLOPS/W or bandwidth numbers; no process node or area estimate. Single-author affiliation (Illumina, a genomics company, not an AI-chip vendor).
previous_facts.project_relevance: Tangentially relevant to the AI-chip-accelerator card: MADAR proposes a genuinely novel architectural mechanism (abolish addresses; all state circulates in compile-time-scheduled rings; distributed collision execution; period hierarchy replaces caches) whose stated payoff is clearest for AI acceleration (MAC compiles to a streaming form with claimed flat energy-per-op as reduction grows; operand reuse routes through the period hierarchy). It addresses the card's question of which bottleneck is targeted: it explicitly targets the data-movement/addressing overhead rather than peak TOPS/TFLOPS. However, it fails the card's primary evidence bar on every dimension: no silicon, no pre-silicon validation against a matched synthesized baseline, no measured throughput/latency/energy-per-op/W, no HBM/interconnect/package data, and the authors themselves state the energy figures are stand-ins and a synthesis-based comparison is the missing evaluation. For the project this is an idea-stage design point worth noting for its mechanism (rotation as memory hierarchy, exact scheduling without reactive memory), not a deployable or benchmarkable AI accelerator result.
